route: The value as an algebraic function of the coin bias: replace the fair coin at every average vertex by bias p, study p |-> val_p on (0,1), and ask whether a continuation from a deterministic endpoint to p = 1/2 crosses few pair-regions.
headline: The route is closed, and closed twice over. (1) LEGITIMACY AND EQUIVALENCE: a dyadic bias k/2^ell is simulated exactly by ell fair average vertices per average vertex (value-exact, stopping-preserving, on arbitrary SSGs), and conversely a FAIR coin is realised inside the p-biased world by a three-vertex von Neumann gadget r->(h,t), h->(r,A), t->(B,r), which delivers exactly 1/2 for EVERY p in (0,1). Hence the p-biased problem is polynomial-time equivalent to SSG-Value at every interior dyadic p and at least as hard at every interior real p; and even lim_{p->0+} val_p is target-equivalent, while val at p=0 itself is linear-time. The homotopy has no easy interior point and no usable germ at the easy endpoints, which are genuine discontinuities (v->(t_1,v) is stopping with val_p = 1 for p>0 and 0 at p=0). (2) THE FOLD IN p: the von Neumann gadget lets one designated coin carry the parameter while the rest of the game is insulated from it, which transports thm:fold from the sink-payoff parameter to the coin bias. The resulting family PDtilde_D (stopping, two-player, N = 14D) has val_p(F_D) = 2^{-(D+1)}((1-p)+1-2^{-D}+2^{-D} T^D(p)) with T the tent map: EXACTLY 2^D affine pieces, breakpoints exactly at j 2^{-D}, slopes alternating 0 and -2^{-D}, all 2^D branches pairwise distinct. So the optimal pair changes 2^{N/14}-1 times, the first breakpoint sits at distance 2^{-N/14} from the endpoint, and any annihilating polynomial P(y,p) has deg_y P >= 2^{N/14}. The straight segment from the corner 0 of [0,1]^a to the centre crosses 2^{D-1} regions, so the multi-parameter shadow-vertex version dies too. (3) The unmodified P_D at uniform bias also folds: the normalised recursion is the skew tent map alpha_d = |alpha_{d-1}-p|/(1-p), and the exact piece counts are 2,4,8,16,29,54,99,183,339,629,1173,2198,4168,7902,15107 for D=1..15 (N <= 92) -- a measurement, growth ratio 1.855..1.912. (4) The phenomenon is INDEPENDENT of every mechanism in sec:gap: WD, CC, H_m, S_r, L_n and the own-successor stall R all have at most TWO pieces in p, while the Z-seeded own-successor hybrid fires at round two on P_D.

results.name: lem:cb-transfer
results.statement: For a bias vector varpi with mu = min_v min(varpi(v),1-varpi(v)) > 0, every result of sec:operators and sec:stopping used here (thm:determinacy, lem:monotone, lem:lfp, thm:lfp-general, lem:trap, thm:eval-stopfree, lem:absorption, thm:contraction, thm:stopping-determinacy, cor:comparison, lem:local-global, thm:opt-subcube) holds for G_varpi with the same proof, the absorption bound of lem:absorption becoming mu^a and the contraction rate 1-mu^a. Moreover the transition kernel has the same SUPPORT as at bias 1/2, so G_varpi and G have identical trap lattices and G_varpi is stopping iff G is, for every varpi with values in (0,1).
results.argument: Every cited proof uses of an average row only that it is a convex combination of the two successor coordinates with both weights positive; 1/2 enters exactly once, in lem:absorption's estimate that a fixed simple path of length <= N-1 is followed with probability >= 2^{-a}, which becomes mu^a. The trap conditions of lem:trapchar are graph conditions, and positivity of both branch probabilities makes the supports coincide.
results.verification: stoppingness computed by the trap fixpoint (both sinks excluded) and cross-checked against exhaustive max-min values on 61 non-stopping and 74 stopping random games.

results.name: lem:cb-dyadic
results.statement: Let G be an ARBITRARY SSG and varpi(v) = k_v 2^{-ell} with 0 < k_v < 2^ell, k_v = sum_i b^v_i 2^{ell-i}. Replace each v in Vavg with successors A = v^(0), B = v^(1) by a chain of ell FAIR average vertices d_1..d_ell, d_1 taking v's place and inheriting its in-edges, with d_i -> ( [b^v_i=1] ? A : B , d_{i+1} ) and d_{ell+1} := B. The result Ghat is a fair-coin SSG with |V(Ghat)| = |V(G)| + (ell-1)a, the same Vmax and Vmin, computable in O(ell N), with v^{Ghat}_{sigma,tau}(u) = v^{varpi}_{sigma,tau}(u) for every positional pair and every u in V(G); hence val_{Ghat} = val_{G_varpi} on V(G). Ghat is stopping iff G is. The vertex count ell is optimal by lem:denominator-sharp.
results.argument: With rho_i := sum_{j>=i} b^v_j 2^{i-1-j} one has rho_{ell+1}=0, rho_i = (b^v_i + rho_{i+1})/2 and rho_1 = varpi(v); first-step analysis gives Pr_{d_1}[exit at A] = rho_1 = varpi(v), and the exit happens within ell steps. The controlled vertices are unchanged, so a positional pair of one game is one of the other, and the chain of Ghat observed at the visits to V(G) is exactly M^{varpi}_{sigma,tau} by the strong Markov property; taking max_sigma min_tau transfers the value. For stopping: a nonempty trap U of Ghat forces, from any chain vertex in U, all later chain vertices and B in U, and (since varpi(v) > 0, so some b^v_j = 1) also A in U; U cap V(G) is then a nonempty trap of G, and conversely a trap of G lifts by adding the chain vertices of its average members.
results.verification: exact: 74 freshly generated random STOPPING SSGs on 9 vertices x 8 dyadic biases (1/4,3/4,1/8,5/8,7/8,11/16,1/32,23/32) = 592 instances, every coordinate of the value vector equal; plus 61 random NON-STOPPING SSGs on 7 vertices with values by exhaustive max_sigma min_tau, 240 checks, 0 failures. Stoppingness agreed in every case.

results.name: lem:cb-vonneumann
results.statement: Replace each v in Vavg of an arbitrary SSG G, with successors A = v^(0), B = v^(1), by three average vertices v, h_v, t_v with v->(h_v,t_v), h_v->(v,A), t_v->(B,v). Then |V(G^vN)| = N + 2a <= 3N, Vmax and Vmin are unchanged, and for EVERY p in (0,1), every positional pair and every u in V(G), v^{(G^vN)_p}_{sigma,tau}(u) = v^{G}_{sigma,tau}(u) (the FAIR value); hence val_{(G^vN)_p} = val_G on V(G), identically in p. G^vN is stopping iff G is.
results.argument: Let x = Pr_v[the token leaves {v,h_v,t_v} at A] at bias p, q = 1-p. First-step analysis: Pr_{h_v} = px+q, Pr_{t_v} = qx, so x = p(px+q) + q(qx), i.e. x(1-p^2-q^2) = pq. Since 1-p^2-q^2 = 2pq and pq > 0, x = 1/2 identically in p; each passage leaves the triple with probability 2pq > 0 so the exit time is a.s. finite. The observed chain on V(G) is therefore the fair chain M_{sigma,tau}; max_sigma min_tau transfers the value. Traps: a trap containing v contains h_v,t_v hence A and B, and a trap containing h_v or t_v contains v. (This is von Neumann 1951 realised as a graph gadget; attributed.)
results.verification: exact: 77 random stopping SSGs at p = 1/7, 2/5, 1/2, 3/4, 9/10, 1/100, 99/100 (539 value-vector comparisons) plus the 61 non-stopping games at p = 1/3, 4/5 by exhaustive max-min; 0 failures. Independently, PDtilde_D matches the closed form of thm:cb-fold at 60 rationals for D = 1..7.

results.name: thm:cb-equivalence + cor:cb-limit + prop:cb-endpoint
results.statement: (i) For every ell, deciding val_{G_varpi}(v0) >= theta for biases in 2^{-ell}Z cap (0,1) reduces in time O(ell N), preserving stoppingness, to the same question on a fair SSG with N + (ell-1)a vertices. (ii) For every real p in (0,1), SSG-Value on N vertices reduces in linear time, preserving stoppingness and the threshold 1/2, to val_{H_p}(v0) >= 1/2 with |V(H)| <= 3N. Hence for every fixed dyadic p in (0,1) of O(log N) bits the p-biased problem is polynomial-time EQUIVALENT to SSG-Value, and for every fixed real p in (0,1) it is at least as hard. Moreover (cor:cb-limit) deciding lim_{p->0+} val_{H_p}(v0) >= 1/2 is at least as hard as SSG-Value, although val_H at p = 0 is a deterministic reachability game solvable in linear time; and (prop:cb-endpoint) p |-> val_p does not extend continuously to p = 0 even on stopping games -- v -> (t_1, v) with v average is stopping with val_p(v) = 1 for all p in (0,1) and value 0 at p = 0.
results.argument: (i) is lem:cb-dyadic, (ii) is lem:cb-vonneumann with H := G^vN. cor:cb-limit is immediate because p |-> val_{(G^vN)_p}(v0) is CONSTANT on (0,1). prop:cb-endpoint: for p > 0 the token leaves v for t_1 with probability 1; {v} is not a trap since t_1 is not in it and v is average, so the game is stopping; at p = 0 the token loops for ever. ATTRIBUTION: (i) is the standard normalisation of the model (Condon 1992 already allows rational transition probabilities; the chain is the Knuth-Yao expansion), (ii) is von Neumann's 1951 unbiasing trick. Neither half is new; their conjunction, and its consequence for the homotopy, is the content.
results.verification: both directions verified exactly as recorded under lem:cb-dyadic and lem:cb-vonneumann; prop:cb-endpoint by exhaustive max-min at p = 1/2, 1/10, 1/1000, 1/10^9.

results.name: lem:cb-piecewise
results.statement: (a) For a fixed positional pair, p |-> v^p_{sigma,tau}(u) = N_u(p)/Delta(p) with Delta = det(I - P_p) taken on the p-INDEPENDENT set R_{sigma,tau} of vertices from which t_1 is reachable; deg Delta <= a, deg N_u <= a, all integer coefficients bounded by 2^a 2^{N/2} (so O(N) bits), and Delta > 0 on (0,1). (b) p |-> val_p(u) is continuous on (0,1). (c) On a stopping game, (0,1) splits into at most 2^{|C|+1}|C| a + 1 open intervals on each of which one pair is optimal throughout and val_p is that pair's rational function.
results.argument: (a) Write I - P_p = M_0 + p M_1 with M_0 = I - Pi_ctrl - R^(1) and M_1 = R^(1) - R^(0); M_1 vanishes on controlled rows and every row of M_0, M_1 has Euclidean norm <= sqrt 2. Expanding the determinant multilinearly in the average rows gives degree <= a and |c_k| <= binom(a,k) 2^{|R|/2} by Hadamard; Cramer transfers the bound to numerators; Delta > 0 by lem:watched since I - P_p restricted to R is I - S with rho(S) < 1. (b) finite max-min of continuous functions. (c) By lem:local-global a pair is optimal at p iff all its Bellman margin numerators m_{pi,v} (degree <= a) are >= 0; off the union B of their zero sets every sign is constant, and |B| <= 2^{|C|}|C| a.
results.verification: degrees and coefficient sizes computed exactly on H_4, WD(4,2,6), P_3, PDtilde_2; the interpolated branches were re-checked against direct exact solves at four extra rationals for every pair used anywhere in the measurements.

results.name: lem:cb-derivative
results.statement: Let G be stopping, p_0 in (0,1), and (sigma,tau) optimal on [p_0, p_0+eps). With N = (I - P_{p_0})^{-1} the Green function of M^{p_0}_{sigma,tau}, for every vertex v: d^+/dp val_p(v) at p_0 equals sum_{u in Vavg} N(v,u) ( w_{p_0}(u^(0)) - w_{p_0}(u^(1)) ), where w_{p_0} = val_{p_0}. Same for the left derivative.
results.argument: On the interval val_p = f_p with f_p = P_p f_p + beta_p on the non-sinks and I - P_p invertible (stopping, lem:absorption). Differentiating, (I - P_p) f_p' = (d_p P_p) f_p + d_p beta_p, whose right-hand side vanishes on controlled rows and equals f_p(u^(0)) - f_p(u^(1)) on the row of an average u. Hence f_p' = N Delta. This is the bias analogue of thm:impedance: the perturbation is the coin rather than a controlled choice and the transfer coefficient is again a Green-function entry. Consequence: the derivative reports exactly the average-vertex successor gaps that def:slack tries to bound, Green-weighted -- the homotopy carries no information not already in those gaps.
results.verification: 248 (game, bias) instances on random stopping SSGs on 10 vertices at p = 1/3, 2/5, 1/2, 3/5, comparing the exact derivative of the interpolated branch with the Green sum; 0 mismatches.

results.name: thm:cb-fold (THE MAIN RESULT)
results.statement: Let PDtilde_D be P_D of thm:fold with every average vertex EXCEPT u replaced by a von Neumann triple (lem:cb-vonneumann). It is a stopping two-player SSG with |V| = 14D, of which 12D-2 are average, D are Max and D are Min. For every p in (0,1), with T(x) = |2x-1|,  val_{PDtilde_D, p}(F_D) = 2^{-(D+1)} ( (1-p) + 1 - 2^{-D} + 2^{-D} T^D(p) ). Hence p |-> val_p(F_D) is piecewise affine with EXACTLY 2^D pieces, breakpoints exactly at j 2^{-D} for 1 <= j <= 2^D - 1, slopes alternating between 0 and -2^{-D}, and its 2^D branches pairwise distinct affine functions. Since N = 14D the number of breakpoints is 2^{N/14} - 1.
results.argument: By lem:cb-vonneumann every replaced average vertex delivers exactly 1/2 to each original successor, for every p, and the controlled vertices are untouched; so for every pair the chain of (PDtilde_D)_p observed at V(P_D) is P_D with fair coins except at u, where the bias is p. Both successors of u are sinks, so val(u) = 1-p under every pair and u is a source of the recursion; hence for every pair and every v != u the profile value equals that of P_D[u := 1-p], and val_{PDtilde_D,p}(F_D) = R_{u,F_D}(1-p). thm:fold evaluates R_{u,F_D}(theta), and T(1-theta) = T(theta) gives T^D(1-p) = T^D(p) for D >= 1. Piece count: T^D is affine on [j2^{-D},(j+1)2^{-D}] with slopes alternating +-2^D, so val_p has slope 2^{-(D+1)}(-1 +- 1) in {0, -2^{-D}}, alternating. Distinctness: on an increasing cell the branch is the constant 2^{-(D+1)}(2 - 2^{-D}(j+1)); on a decreasing cell it is 2^{-(D+1)}(2 - 2^{-D} + 2^{-D}(j+1)) - 2^{-D} p; within each slope class j separates them, and the slope separates the classes. Vertex count: 6D non-sinks of which 4D average; replacing 4D-1 of them adds 2(4D-1), giving 14D-2 non-sinks.
results.verification: exact, on FRESH larger instances: for D = 1..7 (N = 14,28,42,56,70,84,98) the closed form was compared with the value computed by strategy improvement whose output is VERIFIED to be a fixed point of T_p (unique on a stopping game by thm:contraction), at the 60 rationals k/61 and on the dyadic grid and its midpoints; 0 mismatches. The slope set on the 2^D dyadic cells was confirmed to be {0, -2^{-D}} and alternating (explicitly re-run at D = 6 on the correct 2^{-6} cells). Independently, the full 2^{|C|}-envelope method returns exactly 2 and 4 pieces for D = 1, 2.

results.name: cor:cb-continuation
results.statement: On PDtilde_D the optimal pair changes at least 2^{N/14} - 1 times as p sweeps (0,1), and the breakpoint nearest either endpoint sits at distance 2^{-N/14} from it. Hence any method that sweeps the bias and recomputes at each region boundary, or that starts near a deterministic endpoint and follows the optimal pair, costs 2^{Omega(N)}; and the resolution needed merely to take the first step is 2^{-Omega(N)}.
results.argument: Each of the 2^D - 1 breakpoints is a point of non-analyticity of val_p, and on each side val_p coincides with the rational function of an optimal pair; two pairs with the same rational function would make val_p analytic there. The extreme breakpoints are 2^{-D} and 1 - 2^{-D}.
results.verification: follows from thm:cb-fold; the breakpoint locations were also recovered independently by the left-to-right walk (exact brackets 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4, 7/8 at D = 3).

results.name: thm:cb-multi
results.statement: Give PDtilde_D the bias vector varpi_s = s/2, i.e. travel the straight segment in [0,1]^a from the corner 0 (where the game is deterministic and linear-time solvable) to the centre (1/2)*1. Then s |-> val_{varpi_s}(F_D) is piecewise affine with exactly 2^{D-1} pieces on (0,1], with breakpoints at s = j 2^{-(D-1)}, 1 <= j <= 2^{D-1} - 1. So a straight-line homotopy from a solvable corner of [0,1]^a to the all-1/2 point crosses 2^{Omega(N)} pair-regions. Every crossing is transversal (the two branches differ in slope by exactly 2^{-D}), so an open -- but exponentially thin -- neighbourhood of paths crosses at least as many.
results.argument: Along the segment every coordinate equals s/2, so the game is (PDtilde_D)_p with p = s/2 in (0,1/2]; thm:cb-fold applies and the breakpoints j2^{-D} with j < 2^{D-1} pull back to s = j2^{-(D-1)}.
results.verification: exact, full-envelope method: PDtilde_3 gives exactly 4 = 2^{D-1} pieces. On the unmodified P_D the all-0 and all-1 corners give 1, 2, 4, 8 pieces at D = 1,2,3,4, while three random corners of {0,1}^a at D = 4 give 3, 3 and 4 -- so the count DOES degrade for a generic corner, which is reported as such.

results.name: prop:cb-degree + rem:cb-elimination
results.statement: If P in Z[y,p], P != 0, satisfies P(val_p(v0), p) = 0 for all p in (0,1), then deg_y P is at least the number of distinct branches of val_.(v0). On PDtilde_D this gives deg_y P >= 2^D = 2^{N/14}. The product over pairs of (Delta_{sigma tau}(p) y - N_{sigma tau}(p)) is such a polynomial, of y-degree 2^{|C|}, p-degree <= 2^{|C|} a and coefficient length 2^{O(N)} * 2^{|C|} bits. Locally the opposite holds: on each piece the value is a RATIONAL function of p of degree <= a with O(N)-bit coefficients, so the germ at p = 1/2 has y-degree one -- and naming it is naming the optimal pair, which is target-equivalent by thm:transport-objective.
results.argument: For each branch r_i in Q(p), P(r_i(p),p) vanishes on an interval hence identically, so r_i is a root of P in Q(p)[y]; distinct branches give distinct roots. thm:cb-fold supplies 2^D pairwise distinct affine branches. Hence the resultant/elimination blow-up in the algebraic-function route is INTRINSIC, not an artefact of the elimination order: no reorganisation of the elimination of the 2^{|C|} sign patterns of the Bellman disjunctions avoids y-degree 2^{Omega(N)}.
results.verification: the distinctness of the 2^D branches is proved explicitly inside thm:cb-fold and confirmed by the measured 2^D pieces for D <= 3 by the envelope method.

results.name: prop:cb-multiset
results.statement: Two stopping SSGs on 11 vertices, A and B, with M in Vmax, M->(Q_0,Q_1), Q_i in Vmin, Q_i->(c_{i0},c_{i1}), where c_{ij} is a chain of L_{ij} average vertices z_1->(t_0,z_2), ..., z_k->(t_0,t_1), with L^A = [[2,1],[1,2]] and L^B = [[1,1],[2,2]]. For every p in (0,1) the multisets of the eight profile values at M coincide -- hence so do the polynomials prod (y - v^p_{sigma,tau}(M)) -- while val^A_p(M) = q^2 and val^B_p(M) = q differ for every p in (0,1). So the sign of val_{1/2} - 1/2 CANNOT be read off from an annihilating polynomial without further data.
results.argument: A chain of k average vertices as displayed has value q^k. Each entry q^{L_ij} occurs twice among the eight pairs (once per irrelevant choice at the other Min vertex), so the multiset is {q,q,q^2,q^2} doubled in both games; the values are max_i min_j q^{L_ij}, equal to q^2 for L^A and q for L^B.
results.verification: exact at p = 1/7, 3/11, 1/2, 5/6, 97/100: multisets identical in every case, val(A) = q^2 and val(B) = q in every case; both games verified stopping.

results.name: prop:cb-tables
results.statement: Exact piece counts of p |-> val_p(v0) on (0,1) under the uniform bias, by full enumeration of the 2^{|C|} pairs with exact Sturm isolation of every margin numerator and determinant: L_n (n=1..7, N=2n+2): 1 piece, the value is identically 1; H_m: 1 piece for m=1 and 2 pieces for m=2..6; S_r (r=0..6): 1; R of prop:own-stall (N=10, |C|=5): 1; CC(1,2), CC(2,2): 1; CC(1,3), CC(2,3), CC(3,3), CC(2,4), CC(3,4): 2; WD(2j,j,j+4) for j=2..5 (N=6j+9): 2; P_D for D=1..4: 2, 4, 8, 16; PDtilde_D for D=1,2: 2, 4. So EVERY stalling family of the paper has at most two pieces, and the families that fold in p are decided at round two by the Z-seeded own-successor hybrid (measured on P_D, D=1,2,3: it fires at round 2 at every value-distinguishing controlled vertex; D=1 has none).
results.argument: For each game all 2^{|C|} profile vectors were computed as elements of Q(p) by exact interpolation from exact rational evaluations (and re-verified at four fresh rationals); the candidate breakpoints are the real roots in (0,1) of all Bellman-margin numerators and all determinants, isolated by exact Sturm counting; between consecutive candidates every margin has constant sign, so the optimal-pair set is constant and the value is one fixed rational function, recomputed at a rational sample point of each cell. Adjacent cells are merged when their germs at v0 agree.
results.verification: a second, independent left-to-right walk agreed on every entry except P_4, where its interval bookkeeping skipped one of two nearby roots and returned 15 pieces instead of 16; the envelope method is the one reported and it agrees with the independent scalar recursion of prop:cb-PD-uniform on P_1..P_4.

results.name: prop:cb-PD-uniform
results.statement: With ALL coins of P_D at bias p: val_p(k_j) = q^{2D-j}, and with s_d = f_d + g_d, phi_d = f_d - g_d at (F_d, G_d),  s_d = q s_{d-1} + p q^{2d-1},  phi_d = | q phi_{d-1} - p q^{2d-1} |,  s_0 = phi_0 = q,  val_p(F_D) = (s_D + phi_D)/2. Normalising phi_d = q^{2d} alpha_d gives the skew tent map alpha_d = |alpha_{d-1} - p|/q with alpha_0 = q; substituting beta = 1 - alpha, lambda = 1/q gives beta_d = 1 - |1 - lambda beta_{d-1}| with beta_0 = p, the tent map of slope lambda in (1,2] on [0,1] for p in (0,1/2], which at p = 1/2 is the full tent map of thm:fold. MEASURED exact piece counts on (0,1): 2, 4, 8, 16, 29, 54, 99, 183, 339, 629, 1173, 2198, 4168, 7902, 15107 for D = 1..15 (N = 6D+2 <= 92); consecutive ratios lie in [1.855, 1.912] for D = 10..15.
results.argument: The recursion is PROVED: both successors of u are sinks so val_p(u) = q; the chain gives val_p(k_{2D-2d+1}) = q^{2d-1}; P_D is acyclic so backward induction gives val_p(X_d) = q f_{d-1} and val_p(Y_d) = p q^{2d-1} + q g_{d-1}, and f_d, g_d are their max and min, whence max+min = sum and max-min = |difference|. The PIECE COUNT is a measurement: the sign changes of alpha_{d-1}(p) - p were enumerated exactly level by level with rational-coefficient polynomial arithmetic and exact Sturm isolation. No asymptotic lower bound on it is proved; the proved exponential statement is thm:cb-fold.
results.verification: the scalar recursion was checked against the value of the actual game (verified strategy improvement) at 29 rationals for D = 1..4; its piece count agrees with the independent full-envelope count 2,4,8,16 for D = 1..4.

gap: There is a family of stopping ONE-PLAYER SSGs on N vertices such that, with every coin at bias p, the function p |-> val_p(v0) has N^{omega(1)} breakpoints on (0,1). (Not proved here, and not refuted. The fold used by PDtilde_D and P_D is the identity max(x,y) - min(x,y) = |x-y|, which needs BOTH players: in a one-player game the value of a vertex is a monotone function of its successors' values and there is no negation gadget. Every one-player family measured -- L_n, CC, WD -- has at most two pieces. A dedicated search over layered one-player towers, where Max chooses at level i between two average chains transporting the value t of v_{i+1} to q^k t + p sum_{j: X_j = t_1} q^{j-1}, found: over 600 random configurations per depth with chains of length up to 8, maximum exact piece count 1, 3, 4 at depths 1, 2, 3; and a greedy tower built level by level over all 62*61 pairs of chains of length <= 5 reached 2, 3, 5, 7 pieces at depths 1, 2, 3, 4 on N <= 7, 12, 19, 26 vertices -- growth consistent with 2n-1, not with doubling. The architecture is special (one scalar signal), so this is evidence, not a bound.)

Nothing in it depends on any (v1)-(v11) item.

The von Neumann gadget (lem:cb-vonneumann) is a REUSABLE TOOL beyond this route and should be flagged as such: it makes "a fair coin" definable inside any perturbed model at a cost of 3x in a, and it therefore transports EVERY frozen-payoff statement of sec:fold, and every other statement whose parameter can be carried by one designated coin, into the perturbed model. Any future route that perturbs the probabilities (control homotopies, regularisations, smoothings, discounting) should be checked against it FIRST: if the perturbed model can realise an exact fair coin, the perturbation buys nothing and the route is closed before it starts. This is the cheapest available test and it should be run before any further homotopy route is commissioned.

\section{The coin bias as a homotopy parameter}\label{sec:coinbias}

Every average vertex of \Cref{def:ssg} tosses a fair coin. Replacing the
constant $\tfrac12$ by a parameter turns \Cref{prob:main} into a
one-parameter family whose two endpoints are deterministic games, solvable in
linear time by attractor sweeps, and whose midpoint is the target. This
section settles what the family is worth. Three things are proved: the family
is legitimate (a biased coin is simulated exactly by fair ones, and
conversely); it is \emph{target-equivalent at every interior parameter}, so
there is no easy region to start a continuation from except the two endpoints;
and the optimal pair changes $2^{\Omega(N)}$ times along the path, on a
stopping two-player game, so no continuation that tracks the pair is
polynomial. This closes the route in the form that motivates it, exactly as
\Cref{thm:fold} closes the sink-payoff continuation.

\subsection{The biased game and its legitimacy}

\begin{definition}[Biased game]\label{def:cb-bias}
Let $G$ be an SSG and $\varpi\colon\Vavg\to(0,1)$. The \emph{biased game}
$G_\varpi$ has the same graph, the same $\Vmax,\Vmin,\Vavg$ and the same sinks
as $G$; a token at $v\in\Vavg$ moves to $v^{(0)}$ with probability $\varpi(v)$
and to $v^{(1)}$ with probability $1-\varpi(v)$. Strategies, profile values
$v^{\varpi}_{\sigma,\tau}$, $\val_\varpi$ and the Shapley operator $T_\varpi$
are defined verbatim as in \Cref{def:strategies,def:shapley}. We write $G_p$
and $\val_p$ for the \emph{uniform} case $\varpi\equiv p$, and $q:=1-p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The theory transfers]\label{lem:cb-transfer}
Fix $\varpi$ with $\mu:=\min_{v}\min(\varpi(v),1-\varpi(v))>0$. Then
\Cref{thm:determinacy,lem:monotone,lem:lfp,thm:lfp-general,lem:trap,%
thm:eval-stopfree,lem:absorption,thm:contraction,thm:stopping-determinacy,%
cor:comparison,lem:local-global,thm:opt-subcube} hold for $G_\varpi$ with the
same proofs, the only quantitative change being that the absorption bound of
\Cref{lem:absorption} becomes $\mu^{a}$ and the contraction rate of
\Cref{thm:contraction} becomes $1-\mu^{a}$. Moreover the support of the
transition kernel of $M^{\varpi}_{\sigma,\tau}$ equals that of
$M_{\sigma,\tau}$ for every pair, so $G_\varpi$ and $G$ have the same traps
in the sense of \Cref{lem:trapchar}; in particular
\[
  G_\varpi \text{ is stopping} \iff G \text{ is stopping},
\]
and this does not depend on $\varpi$ as long as every bias lies in $(0,1)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every proof cited uses of the average rows only that they are convex
combinations of the two successor coordinates with \emph{both} weights
positive; the weight $\tfrac12$ enters exactly once, in the estimate of
\Cref{lem:absorption} that a fixed simple path of length $\le N-1$ is followed
with probability at least $2^{-a}$, and with biases $\varpi$ the same path is
followed with probability at least $\mu^{a}$. For the second sentence, a
transition of $M^{\varpi}_{\sigma,\tau}$ has positive probability iff the
corresponding transition of $M_{\sigma,\tau}$ does, because
$\varpi(v),1-\varpi(v)>0$; the trap conditions of \Cref{lem:trapchar} refer
only to the graph, so the trap lattices coincide.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A dyadic bias is $\ell$ fair coins]\label{lem:cb-dyadic}
Let $G$ be an arbitrary SSG, $\ell\ge1$, and let
$\varpi(v)=k_v2^{-\ell}$ with $0<k_v<2^{\ell}$ for every $v\in\Vavg$. Write
$k_v=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}b^{v}_i2^{\ell-i}$ in binary. Let $\widehat G$ be the
SSG obtained from $G$ by replacing each $v\in\Vavg$, with successors
$A:=v^{(0)}$ and $B:=v^{(1)}$, by a chain of $\ell$ fair average vertices
$d^v_1,\dots,d^v_\ell$, where $d^v_1$ occupies the place of $v$ (it inherits
all in-edges of $v$) and
\[
  d^v_i\;\longrightarrow\;\bigl(\,[\,b^v_i{=}1\,]\,?\,A:B\;,\;\;d^v_{i+1}\,\bigr)
  \quad(1\le i\le \ell),\qquad d^v_{\ell+1}:=B .
\]
Then $\widehat G$ is an SSG with fair coins,
$|V(\widehat G)|=|V(G)|+(\ell-1)\,a$, the same $\Vmax$ and $\Vmin$ (hence the
same strategy spaces), it is computable in time $O(\ell N)$, and
\[
  v^{\widehat G}_{\sigma,\tau}(u)\;=\;v^{\varpi}_{\sigma,\tau}(u)
  \qquad\text{for every positional pair and every } u\in V(G),
\]
so $\val_{\widehat G}=\val_{G_\varpi}$ on $V(G)$. Finally $\widehat G$ is
stopping if and only if $G$ is.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Put $\rho_i:=\sum_{j\ge i}b^v_j2^{\,i-1-j}$, so $\rho_{\ell+1}=0$,
$\rho_i=\tfrac12(b^v_i+\rho_{i+1})$ and $\rho_1=\varpi(v)$. Started at
$d^v_i$, the token leaves $\{d^v_1,\dots,d^v_\ell\}$ within $\ell-i+1$ steps,
and first-step analysis for the exit distribution gives
$\Pr_{d^v_i}[\text{exit at }A]=\tfrac12 b^v_i+\tfrac12\Pr_{d^v_{i+1}}[\text{exit
at }A]$, whence $\Pr_{d^v_1}[\text{exit at }A]=\rho_1=\varpi(v)$ and
$\Pr_{d^v_1}[\text{exit at }B]=1-\varpi(v)$. The controlled vertices of
$\widehat G$ are those of $G$, so a positional pair of one game is a
positional pair of the other. Fix such a pair. The chain
$M^{\widehat G}_{\sigma,\tau}$ observed at the successive visits to $V(G)$ is,
by the strong Markov property and the previous sentence, exactly
$M^{\varpi}_{\sigma,\tau}$; the two chains reach $t_1$ from $u\in V(G)$ with
the same probability. Taking $\max_\sigma\min_\tau$ gives the value identity.

For stopping, recall \Cref{lem:trapchar}: a trap misses both sinks, every
average vertex of it has both successors in it and every controlled vertex
some. Let $U\ne\emptyset$ be a trap of $\widehat G$ and put $U_0:=U\cap V(G)$.
If $d^v_i\in U$ for some $i$ then, since the second successor of $d^v_i$ is
$d^v_{i+1}$ and $d^v_{\ell+1}=B$, induction along the chain gives $d^v_j\in U$
for all $j\ge i$ and $B\in U$. If moreover $d^v_1\in U$ then all $d^v_j$ lie
in $U$, and since $0<\varpi(v)$ some $b^v_j=1$, whose first successor is $A$;
so $A\in U$ too. As $U$ misses the sinks, $A$ and $B$ are non-sinks, so
$A,B\in U_0$. Hence: for $v\in\Vavg\cap U_0$ (that is, $d^v_1=v\in U$) both
successors of $v$ lie in $U_0$; for controlled $v\in U_0$ the successor
witnessing the condition in $\widehat G$ is an original vertex, because the
head $d^w_1$ of a chain \emph{is} the original vertex $w$. And
$U_0\ne\emptyset$: if $U$ contains any chain vertex then $B\in U_0$, and
otherwise $U_0=U\ne\emptyset$. So $U_0$ is a nonempty trap of $G$. Conversely,
if $U_0$ is a nonempty trap of $G$ then
$U_0\cup\{d^v_i: v\in\Vavg\cap U_0,\,1\le i\le\ell\}$ is a nonempty trap of
$\widehat G$, since each $d^v_i$ has both successors among
$\{A,B,d^v_{i+1}\}\subseteq U$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-dyadic}
\Cref{lem:cb-dyadic} is the standard normalisation of the model: Condon's
formulation already allows rational transition probabilities and reduces them
to the binary fair form, and the chain above is the Knuth--Yao expansion of a
dyadic probability. It is recorded here only because the route needs the exact
size cost, which is $\ell$ fresh \emph{average} vertices per average vertex ---
so $a$ is multiplied by $\ell$, and any bound whose parameter is $a$
(\Cref{thm:few-avg}, \Cref{thm:escape-class}) must be applied before the
simulation, not after. The count is optimal: by
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp} a gadget with $r$ average vertices realises only
probabilities whose denominator divides an integer $\le 2^{r}$, so $\ell$
vertices are necessary for a general $\ell$-bit dyadic bias.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[A fair coin out of $p$-coins]\label{lem:cb-vonneumann}
Let $G$ be an arbitrary SSG. Let $G^{\mathrm{vN}}$ be obtained by replacing each
$v\in\Vavg$, with successors $A:=v^{(0)},B:=v^{(1)}$, by three average
vertices $v,h_v,t_v$ (the vertex $v$ keeping its in-edges):
\[
  v\longrightarrow(h_v,\,t_v),\qquad
  h_v\longrightarrow(v,\,A),\qquad
  t_v\longrightarrow(B,\,v).
\]
Then $|V(G^{\mathrm{vN}})|=N+2a\le 3N$, $\Vmax$ and $\Vmin$ are unchanged, and for
\emph{every} $p\in(0,1)$, every positional pair and every $u\in V(G)$,
\[
  v^{\,(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p}_{\sigma,\tau}(u)\;=\;v^{\,G}_{\sigma,\tau}(u),
  \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
  \val_{(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p}\big|_{V(G)}=\val_{G} .
\]
Moreover $G^{\mathrm{vN}}$ is stopping if and only if $G$ is.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $q=1-p$ and let $x:=\Pr_{v}[\text{the token leaves }\{v,h_v,t_v\}\text{
at }A]$ in $(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p$. First-step analysis gives
$\Pr_{h_v}[\,\cdot\,]=px+q$ and $\Pr_{t_v}[\,\cdot\,]=qx$, so
$x=p(px+q)+q\,qx$, i.e.\ $x\,(1-p^{2}-q^{2})=pq$. Since $1-p^{2}-q^{2}=2pq$
and $pq>0$, $x=\tfrac12$, identically in $p$. Each passage through $v$ leaves
the triple with probability $2pq>0$, so the exit time is almost surely finite.
The controlled vertices are unchanged, so a positional pair of one game is one
of the other; the chain $M^{(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p}_{\sigma,\tau}$ observed at the visits
to $V(G)$ is $M_{\sigma,\tau}$ (fair), which gives the identity, and
$\max_\sigma\min_\tau$ gives the value statement. The trap argument is that of
\Cref{lem:cb-dyadic}: a trap containing $v$ contains $h_v,t_v$ and hence $A$
and $B$, and a trap containing $h_v$ or $t_v$ contains $v$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Every interior bias is the target]\label{thm:cb-equivalence}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item For every $\ell\ge1$, the problem ``given an SSG $G$, a start vertex
  $v_0$, a bias $\varpi$ with values in $2^{-\ell}\mathbb Z\cap(0,1)$ and a
  rational $\theta$, decide $\val_{G_\varpi}(v_0)\ge\theta$'' reduces, in time
  $O(\ell N)$ and preserving stoppingness, to the same question on a fair SSG
  with $N+(\ell-1)a$ vertices.
\item For every real $p\in(0,1)$, \textsc{SSG-Value} on $N$ vertices reduces,
  in linear time and preserving stoppingness and the threshold $\tfrac12$, to
  the question $\val_{H_p}(v_0)\ge\tfrac12$ for a game $H$ on at most $3N$
  vertices.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, for every fixed dyadic $p\in(0,1)$ of $\ell=O(\log N)$ bits the
$p$-biased value problem is polynomial-time equivalent to \textsc{SSG-Value},
and for every fixed real $p\in(0,1)$ it is at least as hard.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) is \Cref{lem:cb-dyadic}; (ii) is \Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann} with
$H:=G^{\mathrm{vN}}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Even the germ at the singular endpoint is the
target]\label{cor:cb-limit}
For every SSG $G$ and every $p\in(0,1)$, $\val_{(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p}=\val_G$ on
$V(G)$; hence
$\lim_{p\to0^{+}}\val_{(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p}(v_0)=\val_G(v_0)$. Consequently the
problem ``given an SSG $H$ and $v_0$, decide
$\lim_{p\to0^{+}}\val_{H_p}(v_0)\ge\tfrac12$'' is at least as hard as
\textsc{SSG-Value}, although the value of $H$ \emph{at} $p=0$ --- a
deterministic reachability game --- is computable in linear time.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Immediate from \Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann}: the function $p\mapsto
\val_{(G^{\mathrm{vN}})_p}(v_0)$ is constant on $(0,1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-equivalence}
Neither half is new --- (i) is the normalisation of the model and (ii) is von
Neumann's 1951 trick for extracting unbiased bits from a biased coin, here
written as a three-vertex gadget --- but their conjunction is what the
homotopy route needs, and it is destructive for it. The map
$p\mapsto \textsc{SSG-Value}_p$ is constant in difficulty on the open
interval: every interior parameter is target-equivalent, by
\Cref{thm:compare-equivalence} and \Cref{thm:cb-equivalence} together. The
only tractable parameters are the two endpoints, where the game degenerates to
a deterministic reachability game; and the degeneration is a genuine
singularity, not a limit --- see \Cref{prop:cb-endpoint}. A continuation in
$p$ therefore cannot begin at an ``easy'' interior point; it must start at an
endpoint at which $\val$ is discontinuous, and by \Cref{cor:cb-limit} even the
one-sided limit there is target-equivalent, so nothing is gained by taking the
germ instead of a point.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The endpoints are singular]\label{prop:cb-endpoint}
There is a stopping SSG on $3$ vertices, namely $v\to(t_1,v)$ with
$v\in\Vavg$, with $\val_p(v)=1$ for every $p\in(0,1)$ while the deterministic
game at $p=0$ has value $0$. Hence $p\mapsto\val_p$ does not extend
continuously to $p=0$, even on stopping games; the mirror-image game
$v\to(v,t_1)$ does the same at $p=1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $p>0$ the token leaves $v$ for $t_1$ with probability $1$, so
$\val_p(v)=1$; the set $\{v\}$ is not a trap because $t_1\notin\{v\}$ and $v$
is average with a successor outside, so the game is stopping. At $p=0$ the
token loops at $v$ for ever and Min wins.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The value as a function of the bias}

\begin{lemma}[Piecewise rational, with explicit bounds]\label{lem:cb-piecewise}
Let $G$ be an SSG with $a$ average vertices and $C=\Vmax\cup\Vmin$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item For every positional pair $(\sigma,\tau)$ and every $u$, the function
  $p\mapsto v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}(u)$ is a rational function
  $N_u(p)/\Delta(p)$ with integer coefficients, where $\Delta=\det(I-P_p)$ is
  the determinant of the chain restricted to the set $R_{\sigma,\tau}$ of
  vertices from which $t_1$ is reachable --- a set independent of
  $p\in(0,1)$. One has $\deg\Delta\le a$, $\deg N_u\le a$, all coefficients of
  absolute value at most $2^{a}\,2^{N/2}$, and $\Delta(p)>0$ on $(0,1)$. In
  particular each branch is analytic and $1$-bounded on $(0,1)$ and its
  coefficients have $O(N)$ bits.
\item $p\mapsto\val_p(u)$ is continuous on $(0,1)$.
\item If $G$ is stopping, then $(0,1)$ is the disjoint union of finitely many
  open intervals and finitely many points such that on each interval a single
  pair is optimal throughout and $\val_p$ agrees with that pair's rational
  function. The number of such intervals is at most $2^{|C|+1}|C|\,a+1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) On $R:=R_{\sigma,\tau}$ the vector $f:=v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}|_R$ solves
$(I-P_p)f=\beta_p$ where $\beta_p(u)$ is the one-step probability of entering
$t_1$; off $R$ the value is $0$. Positivity of both branch probabilities makes
$R$ the same set for all $p\in(0,1)$. Write $I-P_p=M_0+pM_1$ with
$M_0:=I-\Pi_{\mathrm{ctrl}}-R^{(1)}$ and $M_1:=R^{(1)}-R^{(0)}$, where
$R^{(i)}$ routes each average vertex to its $i$-th successor and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ routes each controlled vertex to its chosen successor;
$M_1$ vanishes on controlled rows and every row of $M_0,M_1$ has Euclidean
norm at most $\sqrt2$. Expanding the determinant multilinearly in the average
rows, $\Delta(p)=\sum_{k\le a}c_kp^{k}$ with
$|c_k|\le\binom ak\,2^{|R|/2}\le 2^{a}2^{N/2}$ by Hadamard's inequality, and
the same bound holds for the numerators obtained by Cramer's rule. The matrix
$I-P_p$ restricted to $R$ is $I-S$ with $S$ substochastic of spectral radius
$<1$, so $\Delta>0$ by \Cref{lem:watched}.

(b) Each $v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}(u)$ is continuous on $(0,1)$ by (a), and
$\val_p=\max_\sigma\min_\tau v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}$ is a finite max--min of
continuous functions.

(c) For a pair $\pi$ and a controlled vertex $v$ let
$m_{\pi,v}(p):=N^{\pi}_{\pi(v)}(p)-N^{\pi}_{\bar\pi(v)}(p)$ at a Max vertex
and the negative of that at a Min vertex; $\deg m_{\pi,v}\le a$. By
\Cref{lem:local-global} on a stopping game, $\pi$ is optimal at $p$ if and only
if $m_{\pi,v}(p)\ge0$ for every controlled $v$ (recall $\Delta^{\pi}>0$).
Let $\mathcal B\subset(0,1)$ be the union of the zero sets of those
$m_{\pi,v}$ that are not identically zero; $|\mathcal B|\le 2^{|C|}|C|\,a$.
On each connected component of $(0,1)\setminus\mathcal B$ every $m_{\pi,v}$ has
a constant sign, so the set of optimal pairs is constant and $\val_p$ agrees
with the rational function of any one of them.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The derivative in the bias]\label{lem:cb-derivative}
Let $G$ be stopping, $p_0\in(0,1)$, and let $(\sigma,\tau)$ be optimal on
$[p_0,p_0+\varepsilon)$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, with Green function
$\mathcal N:=(I-P_{p_0})^{-1}=\sum_{k\ge0}P_{p_0}^{k}$ of
$M^{p_0}_{\sigma,\tau}$. Then for every vertex $v$
\[
  \frac{\partial^{+}}{\partial p}\,\val_p(v)\Big|_{p=p_0}
  \;=\;\sum_{u\in\Vavg}\mathcal N(v,u)\,
        \bigl(w_{p_0}(u^{(0)})-w_{p_0}(u^{(1)})\bigr),
\]
where $w_{p_0}=\val_{p_0}$, and the analogous formula holds for the left
derivative with the pair optimal on $(p_0-\varepsilon,p_0]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the interval in question $\val_p=f_p$ where $f_p=P_pf_p+\beta_p$ on the
non-sinks; the game being stopping, $I-P_p$ is invertible there
(\Cref{lem:absorption}) and $f_p$ is a rational function of $p$ with
$\det(I-P_p)>0$, hence differentiable.
Differentiating, $(I-P_{p})f_p'=(\partial_pP_p)f_p+\partial_p\beta_p$. The
right-hand side vanishes on controlled rows, and on the row of $u\in\Vavg$ it
equals $f_p(u^{(0)})-f_p(u^{(1)})$ with the sink values $0,1$ inserted where
appropriate. Hence $f_p'=\mathcal N\Delta$ with $\Delta$ as displayed.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-derivative}
\Cref{lem:cb-derivative} is the bias analogue of \Cref{thm:impedance}: the
perturbation is the coin rather than a controlled choice, and the transfer
coefficient is again a Green-function entry. Two consequences. First, the
quantity the derivative reports is precisely the vector of average-vertex
successor gaps $w^{\ast}(u^{(0)})-w^{\ast}(u^{(1)})$, the same data the slack
calculus (\Cref{def:slack}) tries to bound, weighted by expected visit counts;
so the homotopy carries no information that is not already in those gaps.
Second, $\sum_u\mathcal N(v,u)$ is the expected absorption time of the chain,
for which the only general bound available is $N2^{a}$ (\Cref{lem:absorption});
so the formula yields no polynomial bound on the derivative, and a homotopy
step size cannot be read off from local data. What replaces such a bound here
is \Cref{cor:cb-continuation}: the first breakpoint can sit at distance
$2^{-\Omega(N)}$ from the endpoint.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The fold in the bias: $2^{\Omega(N)}$ breakpoints}

\begin{definition}[The bias fold $\widetilde P_D$]\label{def:cb-fold}
Let $P_D$ be the game of \Cref{thm:fold}. Let $\widetilde P_D$ be obtained
from $P_D$ by applying the substitution of \Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann} to every
average vertex \emph{except} $u$; that is, every one of
$k_1,\dots,k_{2D-1},X_1,Y_1,\dots,X_D,Y_D$ is replaced by a von Neumann
triple, while $u\to(t_0,t_1)$, $F_d\in\Vmax$ and $G_d\in\Vmin$ are left alone.
Then $\widetilde P_D$ has $|V|=14D$ vertices, of which $12D-2$ are average,
$D$ are Max and $D$ are Min, and it is stopping.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The bias homotopy folds]\label{thm:cb-fold}
Let $D\ge1$ and let $T(x)=|2x-1|$ be the tent map. For every $p\in(0,1)$,
\[
  \val_{\widetilde P_D,\,p}(F_D)
  \;=\;2^{-(D+1)}\Bigl(\,(1-p)+1-2^{-D}+2^{-D}\,T^{D}(p)\,\Bigr).
\]
Consequently $p\mapsto\val_{p}(F_D)$ is piecewise affine with exactly $2^{D}$
pieces, its breakpoints are exactly the dyadic rationals $j2^{-D}$,
$1\le j\le 2^{D}-1$, its slopes alternate between $0$ and $-2^{-D}$, and its
$2^{D}$ branches are pairwise distinct affine functions. Since $N=14D$, the
number of breakpoints is $2^{N/14}-1=2^{\Omega(N)}$ on a \emph{stopping
two-player} SSG.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann} each replaced average vertex delivers exactly
$\tfrac12$ to each of its two original successors, for every $p\in(0,1)$, and
the controlled vertices are untouched; so for every positional pair the chain
of $(\widetilde P_D)_p$ observed at $V(P_D)$ is the chain of $P_D$ with fair
coins everywhere except at $u$, where the bias is $p$. The vertex $u$ has both
successors in $\{t_0,t_1\}$ and no in-edge from itself, so under every pair its
value is $p\cdot0+(1-p)\cdot1=1-p$ and it is a source of the recursion.
Therefore, for every pair and every $v\ne u$,
$v^{(\widetilde P_D)_p}_{\sigma,\tau}(v)=v^{P_D[u:=1-p]}_{\sigma,\tau}(v)$,
and taking $\max_\sigma\min_\tau$,
$\val_{\widetilde P_D,p}(F_D)=R_{u,F_D}(1-p)$ in the notation of
\Cref{sec:fold}. \Cref{thm:fold} evaluates $R_{u,F_D}(\theta)$, and
$T(1-\theta)=|2(1-\theta)-1|=|1-2\theta|=T(\theta)$ gives
$T^{D}(1-p)=T^{D}(p)$ for $D\ge1$; substituting $\theta=1-p$ yields the
displayed formula.

For the piece count, $T^{D}$ is affine exactly on the intervals
$[j2^{-D},(j+1)2^{-D}]$ with slopes alternating between $+2^{D}$ and
$-2^{D}$ (\Cref{thm:fold}), so $\val_p(F_D)$ has slope
$2^{-(D+1)}(-1\pm1)\in\{0,-2^{-D}\}$, alternating; consecutive pieces differ,
so the count is exactly $2^{D}$. For distinctness, on $I_j:=[j2^{-D},(j+1)2^{-D}]$
either $T^{D}(p)=2^{D}p-j$ (increasing) or $T^{D}(p)=(j+1)-2^{D}p$
(decreasing), and substituting,
\[
  \val_p(F_D)\big|_{I_j}=
  \begin{cases}
    2^{-(D+1)}\bigl(2-2^{-D}(j+1)\bigr), & T^{D}\ \text{increasing on } I_j,\\[2pt]
    2^{-(D+1)}\bigl(2-2^{-D}+2^{-D}(j+1)\bigr)-2^{-D}p, & T^{D}\ \text{decreasing on } I_j .
  \end{cases}
\]
Within each of the two slope classes the branches are separated by $j$, and
the two classes are separated by the slope; so the $2^{D}$ branches are
pairwise distinct affine functions of $p$.

The vertex count: $P_D$ has $6D$ non-sinks, $4D$ of them average; replacing
$4D-1$ of those by triples adds $2(4D-1)$ vertices, giving $6D+8D-2=14D-2$
non-sinks and $|V|=14D$; the average vertices are $3(4D-1)+1=12D-2$.
Stoppingness is \Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann} together with the stoppingness of
$P_D$ (\Cref{thm:fold}).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No pair-tracking continuation in the bias is
polynomial]\label{cor:cb-continuation}
On $\widetilde P_D$ the optimal pair changes at least $2^{N/14}-1$ times as
$p$ sweeps $(0,1)$, and the breakpoint nearest to either endpoint is at
distance $2^{-N/14}$ from it. Hence any method that sweeps the bias and
recomputes at each region boundary, or that starts near a deterministic
endpoint and follows the optimal pair, costs $2^{\Omega(N)}$; and the
resolution required merely to make the first step is $2^{-\Omega(N)}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Each of the $2^{D}-1$ breakpoints is a point of non-analyticity of $\val_p$,
and on each side $\val_p$ coincides with the rational function of an optimal
pair; two pairs with the same rational function would make $\val_p$ analytic
there. The extreme breakpoints are $2^{-D}$ and $1-2^{-D}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-fold}
\Cref{thm:cb-fold} answers, in the negative, the question that motivates the
route, and it does so for the parameter that \Cref{thm:fold} does \emph{not}
cover: \Cref{thm:fold} folds the \emph{sink payoff} at a frozen vertex, which
is not a parameter of \Cref{def:ssg} at all, whereas $p$ is. The bridge is
\Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann}: it makes ``fair'' a definable notion inside the
$p$-biased world, so that a single designated coin can carry the parameter
while the rest of the game is insulated from it. The same device transports
\emph{any} statement about the frozen-payoff homotopy to the bias homotopy at
a cost of a factor $3$ in $a$.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Multi-parameter: a corner-to-centre segment
folds]\label{thm:cb-multi}
Give $\widetilde P_D$ the bias vector $\varpi_s\equiv s/2$ obtained by
travelling along the straight segment in $[0,1]^{a}$ from the corner
$\mathbf 0$ --- where the game is deterministic and solvable by attractor
sweeps in linear time --- to the centre $\tfrac12\mathbf 1$. Then
$s\mapsto\val_{\varpi_s}(F_D)$ is piecewise affine with exactly $2^{D-1}$
pieces on $(0,1]$, with breakpoints at $s=j2^{-(D-1)}$, $1\le j\le
2^{D-1}-1$. Hence a straight-line homotopy from a solvable corner of
$[0,1]^{a}$ to the all-$\tfrac12$ point crosses $2^{\Omega(N)}$ pair-regions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Along the segment every coordinate equals $s/2$, so the game is
$(\widetilde P_D)_{p}$ with $p=s/2\in(0,\tfrac12]$ and
\Cref{thm:cb-fold} applies; the breakpoints $j2^{-D}$ with $j<2^{D-1}$ pull
back to $s=j2^{-(D-1)}$, and there are $2^{D-1}-1$ of them in $(0,1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-multi}
At every breakpoint the two branches differ in slope by exactly $2^{-D}$, so
each crossing is transversal; transversality is an open condition, so every
path in a $C^{1}$-neighbourhood of the segment crosses at least as many
regions. The neighbourhood is exponentially thin, which is the honest reading:
this is a statement about a fixed segment plus a perturbation of size
$2^{-\Omega(N)}$, not about a generic segment. What the measurements below add
is that the count degrades under a generic \emph{corner}: on $P_D$ with
$D=4$ the all-$0$ and all-$1$ corners give $8$ regions, while three random
corners of $\{0,1\}^{a}$ give $3$, $3$ and $4$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The algebraic-function reading}

\begin{proposition}[Any annihilating polynomial is
exponential]\label{prop:cb-degree}
Let $G$ be an SSG, $v_0$ a vertex, and $P\in\mathbb Z[y,p]$, $P\ne0$, with
$P(\val_p(v_0),p)=0$ for all $p\in(0,1)$. Then $\deg_yP$ is at least the
number of \emph{distinct} branches of $\val_\bullet(v_0)$. On
$\widetilde P_D$ this gives $\deg_yP\ge 2^{D}=2^{N/14}$. The product
$\prod_{(\sigma,\tau)}\bigl(\Delta_{\sigma\tau}(p)y-N_{\sigma\tau}(p)\bigr)$
is such a polynomial, of $y$-degree $2^{|C|}$, $p$-degree at most $2^{|C|}a$
and coefficient length $2^{O(N)}\!\cdot 2^{|C|}$ bits.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $r_1,\dots,r_k\in\mathbb Q(p)$ be the distinct rational functions with
which $\val_\bullet(v_0)$ agrees on the intervals of
\Cref{lem:cb-piecewise}(c). For each $i$, $P(r_i(p),p)$ vanishes on a
nonempty open interval, hence identically as a rational function of $p$;
so $r_i$ is a root of $P$ regarded as a polynomial in $y$ over the field
$\mathbb Q(p)$. Distinct $r_i$ are distinct roots, so $\deg_yP\ge k$. For
$\widetilde P_D$, \Cref{thm:cb-fold} exhibits $k=2^{D}$ pairwise distinct
affine branches. The last sentence is \Cref{lem:cb-piecewise}(a) together with
the fact that $\val_p$ equals some $v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}(v_0)$ at every $p$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-elimination}
This says exactly where the elimination blows up, and that the blow-up is
intrinsic rather than an artefact of the method. The Bellman system
$y_v=\max(y_{v^{(0)}},y_{v^{(1)}})$ at $\Vmax$, $\min$ at $\Vmin$,
$y_v=py_{v^{(0)}}+(1-p)y_{v^{(1)}}$ at $\Vavg$, is a disjunction over
$2^{|C|}$ sign patterns; eliminating $y_v$ for $v\ne v_0$ by resultants must
resolve those disjunctions, and \Cref{prop:cb-degree} shows that no
reorganisation avoids a $y$-degree $2^{\Omega(N)}$. Locally the situation is
the opposite extreme: on each piece the value is a \emph{rational} function of
$p$ of degree $\le a$ with $O(N)$-bit coefficients (\Cref{lem:cb-piecewise}),
so the germ at $p=\tfrac12$ is degree one --- and naming it is naming the
optimal pair, which is target-equivalent by \Cref{thm:transport-objective}.
The algebraic-function reading therefore relocates the difficulty without
reducing it.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The annihilating polynomial does not determine the
value]\label{prop:cb-multiset}
Let $A$ and $B$ be the two SSGs with $M\in\Vmax$, $M\to(Q_0,Q_1)$,
$Q_0,Q_1\in\Vmin$, and $Q_i\to(c_{i0},c_{i1})$ where $c_{ij}$ is a chain of
$L^{A}_{ij}$ (resp.\ $L^{B}_{ij}$) average vertices $z_1\to(t_0,z_2),\dots,
z_k\to(t_0,t_1)$, with
\[
  L^{A}=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
  L^{B}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\2&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both are stopping, on $11$ vertices. For every $p\in(0,1)$ the multisets
$\{v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}(M)\}$ over all positional pairs coincide, hence so do
the polynomials $\prod_{(\sigma,\tau)}\bigl(y-v^{p}_{\sigma,\tau}(M)\bigr)$;
but $\val_p^{A}(M)=q^{2}$ and $\val_p^{B}(M)=q$, which differ for every
$p\in(0,1)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A chain of $k$ average vertices as displayed has value $q^{k}$ at bias $p$.
The profile values at $M$ are the entries $q^{L_{ij}}$, each occurring twice
(once for each irrelevant choice at the other Min vertex), so the multiset is
$\{q,q,q^{2},q^{2}\}$ doubled in both games. The values are
$\max_i\min_j q^{L_{ij}}$, which is $q^{2}$ for $L^{A}$ and $q$ for $L^{B}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cb-tables}
Every stalling family of this paper --- the wedge $WD$, the crosswise chains
$CC$, $H_m$, $S_r$, the ladder $L_n$ and the own-successor stall $R$ --- has
at most \emph{two} pieces. The bias homotopy is therefore not a refinement of
any mechanism recorded in \Cref{sec:gap}: the instances that defeat the slack,
transport, ratio and hybrid calculi are trivial for it, and the instances that
defeat it, $P_D$ and $\widetilde P_D$, are none of them: the $Z$-seeded
own-successor hybrid of \Cref{rem:own-successor} --- read in both directions
at every controlled vertex --- fires at \emph{round two} at every
value-distinguishing controlled vertex of $P_D$ for $D=1,2,3$ (exact
computation; $D=1$ has no distinguishing controlled vertex at all). The two
phenomena are independent, and the fold of \Cref{sec:fold} is the only source
of parametric hardness found on this route.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The unmodified $P_D$ folds in the bias
too]\label{prop:cb-PD-uniform}
Put all coins of $P_D$ at bias $p$. Writing $f_d,g_d$ for the values at
$F_d,G_d$, $s_d=f_d+g_d$ and $\varphi_d=f_d-g_d$, one has
$\val_p(k_j)=q^{2D-j}$ and
\[
  s_d=q\,s_{d-1}+p\,q^{2d-1},\qquad
  \varphi_d=\bigl|\,q\,\varphi_{d-1}-p\,q^{2d-1}\,\bigr|,\qquad
  s_0=\varphi_0=q,
\]
and $\val_p(F_D)=\tfrac12(s_D+\varphi_D)$. Normalising
$\varphi_d=q^{2d}\alpha_d$ turns the fold into the skew tent map
\[
  \alpha_d=\frac{|\alpha_{d-1}-p|}{q},\qquad \alpha_0=q,
\]
which after the substitution $\beta=1-\alpha$, $\lambda=1/q$ is the tent map
$\beta_d=1-|1-\lambda\beta_{d-1}|$ with $\beta_0=p$, of slope $\lambda\in(1,2]$
and turning point $1/\lambda$, mapping $[0,1]$ into itself for
$p\in(0,\tfrac12]$. At $p=\tfrac12$ it is the full tent map, which is exactly
\Cref{thm:fold}. The exact number of pieces of $p\mapsto\val_p(F_D)$ on
$(0,1)$ is
\[
  2,\;4,\;8,\;16,\;29,\;54,\;99,\;183,\;339,\;629,\;1173,\;2198,\;4168,\;
  7902,\;15107
\]
for $D=1,\dots,15$, i.e.\ on $N=6D+2\le92$ vertices; the ratio of consecutive
terms lies between $1.855$ and $1.912$ throughout $D=10,\dots,15$. This is a MEASUREMENT: the
recursion above is proved, and the piece count was obtained from it by exact
root isolation over $\mathbb Q$, but no asymptotic lower bound on it is proved
here. The proved exponential statement is \Cref{thm:cb-fold}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof of the recursion]
Both successors of $u$ are sinks, so $\val_p(u)=q$; and
$\val_p(k_j)=q\val_p(k_{j+1})$ with $\val_p(k_{2D-1})=q$, giving
$\val_p(k_{2D-2d+1})=q^{2d-1}$. Every edge of $P_D$ leads to a sink, to a
later chain vertex or to a strictly lower level, so $P_D$ is acyclic and the
remaining values are computed by backward induction: $\val_p(X_d)=q f_{d-1}$ and
$\val_p(Y_d)=p\,q^{2d-1}+q\,g_{d-1}$, and $f_d,g_d$ are the max and the min of
those two numbers. Adding and subtracting gives the two displayed recursions
($\max+\min$ is the sum, $\max-\min$ the absolute difference), and
$\varphi_{d-1}=q^{2d-2}\alpha_{d-1}$ gives
$\varphi_d=q^{2d-1}|\alpha_{d-1}-p|=q^{2d}\alpha_d$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What was verified, and how]\label{rem:cb-verified}
All computations are in exact rational arithmetic
(\texttt{fractions.Fraction}); polynomials in $p$ are obtained by exact
evaluation at rationals followed by exact interpolation and are then
re-checked at four further rationals; real roots are isolated by exact Sturm
sequences over $\mathbb Q$ with rational brackets. No floating point enters any
claim. Specifically:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.6em]
\item \Cref{lem:cb-dyadic}: on $74$ freshly generated random \emph{stopping}
  SSGs on $9$ vertices and $8$ dyadic biases each ($592$ instances), and on
  $61$ random \emph{non-stopping} SSGs on $7$ vertices with the value computed
  by exhaustive $\max_\sigma\min_\tau$; every coordinate of the value vector
  agreed, and stoppingness agreed in every case.
\item \Cref{lem:cb-vonneumann}: on $77$ random stopping SSGs at the seven
  biases $\tfrac17,\tfrac25,\tfrac12,\tfrac34,\tfrac9{10},\tfrac1{100},
  \tfrac{99}{100}$, and on the same $61$ non-stopping games; every coordinate
  agreed with the fair value.
\item \Cref{lem:cb-derivative}: $248$ (game, bias) instances on random
  stopping SSGs on $10$ vertices at $p\in\{\tfrac13,\tfrac25,\tfrac12,
  \tfrac35\}$, comparing the exact derivative of the interpolated rational
  branch with the Green-function sum; no mismatch.
\item \Cref{thm:cb-fold}: the closed form was checked against the value of the
  game, computed by verified strategy improvement (the returned vector is
  checked to be a fixed point of $T_p$, which on a stopping game determines it
  by \Cref{thm:contraction}), for $D=1,\dots,7$ --- so up to $N=98$ vertices ---
  at $60$ rationals $k/61$ and on the dyadic grid and its midpoints; no
  mismatch. The slope set on the $2^{D}$ dyadic cells was confirmed to be
  $\{0,-2^{-D}\}$ and alternating.
\item \Cref{thm:cb-multi}: on $\widetilde P_3$ the corner-to-centre segment
  gives exactly $4=2^{D-1}$ pieces, by the full $2^{|C|}$-envelope method.
\item \Cref{prop:cb-tables}: by the full-envelope method (all $2^{|C|}$
  pairs, all margin numerators, all determinants). A second, independent
  left-to-right walk agreed on every entry except $P_4$, where its
  interval bookkeeping skipped one of two nearby roots and returned $15$

\item \Cref{prop:cb-multiset}: the two games were checked at

\end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[What is not proved]\label{rem:cb-gap}
Both $\widetilde P_D$ and $P_D$ use one Max and one Min vertex per level, and
the device is the identity $\max(x,y)-\min(x,y)=|x-y|$: the absolute value is
what folds. In a one-player game no such gadget is available --- the value of
a vertex is a monotone function of its successors' values and there is no
negation --- and every one-player family measured above ($L_n$, $CC$, $WD$)
has at most two pieces.

A dedicated search was run. Consider the layered one-player tower: Max
vertices $v_1,\dots,v_n$, and at level $i$ two chains of average vertices from
$v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$, a chain $z_1,\dots,z_k$ with $z_j\to(X_j,z_{j+1})$,
$z_k\to(X_k,v_{i+1})$ and $X_j\in\{t_0,t_1\}$ transporting the value $t$ of
$v_{i+1}$ to $q^{k}t+p\sum_{j:X_j=t_1}q^{\,j-1}$; then
$\val_p(v_i)=\max_c(\alpha^{c}_i\val_p(v_{i+1})+\beta^{c}_i)$ and
$\val_p(v_{n+1})=1$. Over $600$ random configurations per depth with chains of
length up to $8$, the maximum exact piece count was $1,3,4$ at depths
$1,2,3$; a greedy tower built one level at a time over all $62\cdot61$ pairs
of chains of length $\le5$ reached $2,3,5,7$ pieces at depths $1,2,3,4$ on
$N\le7,12,19,26$ vertices --- growth consistent with $2n-1$, not with
doubling. Nothing exponential was found; the architecture is
special (a single scalar signal), and no lower bound is claimed either way.
The missing statement is exactly:

\emph{There is a family of stopping ONE-PLAYER SSGs on $N$ vertices such that,
with every coin at bias $p$, the function $p\mapsto\val_p(v_0)$ has
$N^{\omega(1)}$ breakpoints on $(0,1)$.}
\end{remark}
